open_points.subject: Kernel authority to end an agent session
open_points.text: A09 gives Cabinet Kernel these session operations: “register an agent session; read the session's access; request access to a project”; A11 says “Cabinet Kernel ends a session when its agent session ends.”
open_points.question: Is ending an agent session an operation allowed by Cabinet Kernel's token?
options: Add 'end an agent session' to Kernel's A09 rights
Only the owner may end a session
Treat ending as part of registration rather than a separately authorised operation
open_points.default_guess: Allow Cabinet Kernel to end the session and treat A09's row as accidentally incomplete.

open_points.subject: Registration of a new agent session
open_points.text: A10 says “A call with agent authority is accepted only when ... the session it names is registered”; A11 says “Cabinet Kernel registers a session when its agent session starts.”
open_points.question: How can the registration call succeed when the named session is not registered yet?
options: Exempt registration from the registered-session check
Require a separate authority or bootstrap operation for registration
Permit registration only for identities pre-registered elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Exempt registration from the registered-session check while still checking Kernel's token.

open_points.subject: Project resolution for pointer operations
open_points.text: A10 says “for an operation on a project — the project is in that session's set” and “An operation on a project that names none uses the session's active project”; withdrawal is otherwise described as naming a pointer, not necessarily a project.
open_points.question: For an operation such as withdrawing a pointer, is the checked project derived from the pointer, required explicitly in the request, or taken from the active project when no project id is supplied?
options: Derive the project from the pointer before checking the grant
Require both pointer id and project id and verify they agree
Use the active project when the request has no project id
open_points.default_guess: Derive the project from the pointer and check that project against the session's set without disclosing the pointer first.

open_points.subject: Owner-session idle state
open_points.text: A13's invariant uses “s.last_action”, but M11 says the OwnerSession facts are only “its identity ... the instant it began; its expiry” and describes them as written once.
open_points.question: What fact records the last owner action needed to enforce the 30-minute idle expiry, and does it mutate on the OwnerSession?
options: Add a mutable last-action instant to OwnerSession
Derive last action from another durable or runtime event store
Replace sliding idle expiry with a fixed expiry known at sign-in
open_points.default_guess: Add a mutable last-action instant to the temporary OwnerSession.

open_points.subject: Meaning of owner action for idle expiry
open_points.text: The session ends after “30 minutes without an owner action,” but “owner action” is not defined for this rule.
open_points.question: Which requests reset the 30-minute idle timer: successful authenticated reads, successful changes, confirmations, refused requests, or any request carrying the session?
options: Every successfully authenticated owner-interface request
Only accepted state-changing actions
Every request carrying a valid session, including refused actions
open_points.default_guess: Reset it after every successfully authenticated owner-interface request, including reads but excluding invalid or unauthenticated requests.

open_points.subject: Sign-in lockout window
open_points.text: “After 5 refused sign-ins within 15 minutes, every sign-in ... is refused for the next 15 minutes.”
open_points.question: When does the lockout start, do attempts made during lockout count as new refused sign-ins or extend it, does a successful sign-in clear the earlier failures, and does restart clear the counter?
options: Fixed 15 minutes from the fifth failure; locked attempts do not extend it; success and restart clear failures
Sliding window in which every locked attempt can extend refusal; success clears failures
Persist failures and lockout across restart until their time windows expire
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed lockout from the fifth failure, do not extend it with blocked attempts, clear the counter after success, and lose it on restart.

open_points.subject: One-use confirmation
open_points.text: “A confirmation step ... is valid only in the session that showed it, and once.”
open_points.question: Is a confirmation consumed by the first attempt or only by an accepted change, when does an unused confirmation expire, and may it be retried after a stale revision or import conflict?
options: Consume on any confirmation attempt and expire with the owner session
Consume only when the action commits and allow retries while the session remains valid
Give confirmations a separate short expiry and consume on first attempt
open_points.default_guess: Expire it with the owner session and consume it on the first attempt, successful or not.

open_points.subject: Concurrent publication and withdrawal
open_points.text: A07 serialises “Publishes of one type on one project,” while withdrawal is only said to occur “in one transaction.”
open_points.question: What outcome is required when a publish and a withdrawal of the currently published pointer occur concurrently?
options: Serialize both operations on the project and type, with either transaction order allowed
Give publication precedence
Give withdrawal precedence
Refuse one operation as a concurrency conflict
open_points.default_guess: Serialize both on the project and type and let transaction order determine whether withdrawal succeeds before publication or is refused after supersession.

open_points.subject: Whether Kernel's token is a service token allowed to publish
open_points.text: A08 says both “A pointer is published ... by Cabinet Kernel for the agent” and “No service token has the right to publish or withdraw”; State 0 calls Kernel's credential a service token and A09 grants it those operations.
open_points.question: Does the prohibition on service tokens exclude Cabinet Kernel's service token when it carries agent authority?
options: Yes; Kernel's token is the explicit exception under agent authority
No; Kernel must use a different non-service credential
No token may publish, leaving only the owner
open_points.default_guess: Treat Kernel's service token with agent authority as the explicit exception.

open_points.subject: Reading pointers of a removed artifact type
open_points.text: A22 says removed-type pointers “are listed and read as before,” then says “‘read the latest artifact of a type’ for it [is] refused as an unknown type.”
open_points.question: Which read operations remain available for pointers whose type was removed?
options: Only list-artifacts/history reads remain; latest-by-type is refused
All existing-pointer reads including latest remain available
No read except raw audit or storage inspection remains
open_points.default_guess: Keep them in list-artifacts/history but refuse latest-by-type.

open_points.subject: Reintroducing a removed artifact type
open_points.text: A22 defines adding and removing a type and says “A type never changes its owner service,” but says nothing about adding the same type name again after removal.
open_points.question: May a later release re-declare a removed type, and if so do its old pointers and version sequence become active history for new publishes and withdrawals?
options: Allow re-declaration with the same owner and continue the old version sequence
Once removed, a type name can never return
Allow re-declaration as a fresh vocabulary entry with versions restarting
open_points.default_guess: Allow it only with the same owner service and continue from the highest historical version.

open_points.subject: Meaning of today in audit erasure
open_points.text: A15 says “The date of an erasure is a date not later than today” and separately uses “the start of that date (UTC).”
open_points.question: Is “today” also the UTC calendar date or the owner's Europe/Madrid calendar date?
options: UTC date
Owner's local date
Configured instance date zone
open_points.default_guess: Use the UTC date because the cutoff is explicitly defined in UTC.

open_points.subject: Required Customer mapping during import
open_points.text: A16 says the mapping shows “each Customer the import will make and the projects it will link”; M04 additionally requires the owner to provide each such Customer's name and kind and decide whether the legacy value is its tax id.
open_points.question: Must the mapping display and require confirmation of the new Customer's name, kind, tax-id decision and discarded legacy value, and what validation refuses confirmation when any is missing?
options: Require and show all of those values before confirmation
Infer name and kind from project data and ask only about tax id
Create incomplete Customers and complete them after import
open_points.default_guess: Require and show the name, kind and tax-id mapping for every new Customer before confirmation.

open_points.subject: Malformed import records
open_points.text: A16 refuses “a malformed record” but does not define malformedness.
open_points.question: Which cross-record conditions make an import malformed, including dangling project/customer links, duplicate ids inside the file, duplicate pointer versions, version gaps, multiple published pointers, invalid statuses, missing required facts and inconsistent timestamps?
options: Validate every State 1 model and every State 2 invariant across the whole selected import
Validate only the eventual States 5–6 file schema
Repair or normalise invalid legacy relationships during mapping
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unless the selected data satisfies every model invariant and all relational invariants without repair.

open_points.subject: Namespace of import id conflicts
open_points.text: A16 names as conflicts “a project, room or pointer id production holds” without saying whether identities of different models share one namespace.
open_points.question: Does a room id conflict with an existing project or pointer id having the same text, or only with another room id?
options: Separate identity namespace for each model
One global namespace for every Registry identity
Separate namespaces except for selected explicitly shared identifiers
open_points.default_guess: Use separate namespaces for projects, rooms, pointers and customers.

open_points.subject: Random generation of configured secrets
open_points.text: A17 requires each secret to be “at least 32 bytes generated at random by the owner's vault,” while startup receives only the resulting configured value.
open_points.question: Is random vault generation an external owner obligation, or must Registry verify some property beyond length and inequality?
options: External obligation; Registry checks only length and inequality
Registry accepts only values carrying verifiable generation metadata
Registry estimates entropy and refuses values judged weak
open_points.default_guess: Treat generation provenance as an external obligation and check only length and distinctness at startup.

open_points.subject: Complete startup validation of configuration and store
open_points.text: A17 says “A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start” and that Registry checks “the store,” but defines neither malformed and unknown configuration items nor what store checks must pass.
open_points.question: What exact configuration schema and store conditions are required before serving: reachability, writability, schema version, migrations, integrity and encryption included or excluded?
options: Require a closed configuration schema plus reachable, writable, compatible and integrity-checked store
Check only presence and syntax of named configuration values
Defer store compatibility and integrity failures until the first operation
open_points.default_guess: Require a closed Registry-specific configuration schema and a reachable, writable store at the exact supported schema version.

open_points.subject: Production-backup restore test environment
open_points.text: A18 requires restoring a production backup “into a temporary instance on VM Platform” and in the same rule says “a test instance never receives a production backup”; State 0 defines every non-production instance as a test instance holding no production personal data.
open_points.question: What kind of instance may receive the production backup for the restore test?
options: A specially defined production-trust restore instance that is not a test instance
A test instance despite the earlier prohibition
No instance; test only backup metadata or encryption
open_points.default_guess: Define an isolated temporary restore instance inside the production trust boundary that is not classified as a test instance.

open_points.subject: Daily backup scheduling and failure
open_points.text: A18 says “Once a day the store is backed up” and backups are “kept 30 days” without defining the schedule or failure response.
open_points.question: What is a day and a backup's age, when is deletion performed, what happens after a missed or failed backup, and may Registry continue serving without a successful recent backup?
options: Calendar-day schedule with alert and continued service
Rolling 24-hour deadline that blocks serving or release when missed
External scheduler policy with no Registry-visible consequence
open_points.default_guess: Use a rolling maximum age of 24 hours, alert on failure, and continue serving while the owner repairs it.

open_points.subject: Recovery point after restoring production
open_points.text: A18 says that after restoring a backup the owner repeats erasures made later, but says nothing about every other accepted change after the backup's instant.
open_points.question: Are post-backup creations, corrections, grants, request ids, audit sequence numbers and the migration closure intentionally lost, replayed from another log, or required to be recovered by some other mechanism?
options: Accept loss of every post-backup change except mandatory erasures
Maintain a transaction log and replay every committed change
Restore only from a backup current enough that no accepted change is lost
open_points.default_guess: Accept a recovery point at the backup and separately replay every later erasure before serving.

open_points.subject: Source for replaying erasures after restore
open_points.text: A18 says the owner repeats “every erasure made after the backup's instant, as the owner's retention review recorded it,” while audit entries may themselves have been erased and the governance record's required contents are not defined here.
open_points.question: What authoritative record tells the owner which customer or project erasures to repeat, and what happens if that record is absent or incomplete?
options: A governance record outside Registry must retain each target identity and action
The audit log is authoritative and may not erase entries still needed by retained backups
The restored instance may serve even when erasure replay cannot be proven complete
open_points.default_guess: Require an external governance record containing the target identity and erasure kind for at least the backup-retention period.

open_points.subject: Restore testing at each release versus product boundary
open_points.text: A18 prescribes “Before each release the owner restores the latest backup”; State 0 explicitly excludes “Deploying Registry, its release process and the host's administration.”
open_points.question: Is the pre-release restore test a normative Registry State 2 rule or an external release-process obligation outside this case?
options: External release-process obligation referenced but not implemented by Registry
Registry blocks startup or release until it can verify a restore test
Remove the rule from this case
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an external owner release-process obligation that Registry itself cannot verify.

open_points.subject: Scope of fixed release dependencies
open_points.text: A20 requires a release to name “every dependency it runs with” at an exact version and digest.
open_points.question: Does this include transitive packages, the language runtime, native libraries, operating-system packages, database engine, browser assets and build-only tools, or only direct application packages?
options: All runtime code recursively, including runtime and native/system libraries
All language-level runtime packages, direct and transitive
Only direct application dependencies
open_points.default_guess: Include every direct and transitive runtime package plus the language runtime, but not the host operating system.

open_points.subject: Dependency release rules versus excluded release process
open_points.text: A20 specifies how “A release names every dependency” and how dependencies change; State 0 says Registry's “release process” is explicitly excluded.
open_points.question: Are A20's dependency manifest and digest verification part of Registry's specification or requirements on an external release process?
options: External release-process requirements whose produced manifest Registry consumes
Registry runtime requirements enforced at installation and startup
Out of scope and therefore not normative here
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as requirements on the external release process, with installation verifying the resulting manifest.

open_points.subject: Facts used to recognise a create replay
open_points.text: A01 says a repeated create is recognised by “the same supplied facts” and answers the record “as it stands now,” but M01 and M04 store only the request id, not the original supplied facts, and projects and Customers can later be corrected.
open_points.question: Are replay facts compared with the original creation facts or with the record's current editable facts, and where are original facts retained if that is the intended comparison?
options: Persist an immutable fingerprint or copy of the original supplied facts
Compare against the record's current facts
After a correction, refuse every retry because the original facts are no longer available
open_points.default_guess: Persist an immutable canonical fingerprint of the original supplied facts and return the current record on a match.

open_points.subject: Blank optional values in replay comparison
open_points.text: A01 says supplied facts are compared “as the caller gave them” and Registry “does not normalise them”; A02 says an optional empty or whitespace-only value “is absent.”
open_points.question: For replay comparison, are an omitted optional fact, an empty string and a whitespace-only string equal or different?
options: All are the same absent value after A02 validation
They remain distinct caller representations for replay comparison
Empty and omitted are equal, but whitespace-only strings remain distinct
open_points.default_guess: Apply A02 first and compare all three as absent.

open_points.subject: Replay checks versus current create preconditions
open_points.text: A01 generally says a matching request id “is a repeat” and returns the record, but only for publish explicitly says “The checks of the call come first”; add-room and project/customer creates have current-state refusal rules that may have changed since creation.
open_points.question: Before returning a replay, which current preconditions are rechecked for project, Customer and room creates—for example an archived room's project or a now restricted, ended or erased linked Customer?
options: Authenticate and authorise, then return any matching replay without revalidating current domain preconditions
Recheck every current precondition before replay recognition
Use per-operation rules, with publish and room retries refused when their project is no longer writable
open_points.default_guess: Check authentication and caller authority first, then return a matching replay without revalidating mutable domain facts, except where a rule explicitly says otherwise for publish.

open_points.subject: Definition of whitespace
open_points.text: A02 defines missing as “white space only” and formalises it with “strip(v)” without declaring the character set or algorithm.
open_points.question: Which characters count as whitespace for blank-value validation?
options: The complete Unicode White_Space property at the specification's fixed Unicode version
ASCII spaces, tabs and line breaks only
The implementation language's current strip function
open_points.default_guess: Use the Unicode White_Space property at a fixed Unicode version.

open_points.subject: Revision result of terminal erasure
open_points.text: A04 includes “erasing a project” and “erasing [a Customer's] contact data” among revision-moving actions, while its invariant says every accepted changed record gets “revision' = revision + 1”; M01 and M04 say those terminal results keep no revision, or the project is deleted whole.
open_points.question: Does terminal erasure increment a revision before removing it, retain the incremented revision, or consume the stated revision without producing a next revision?
options: Require the current revision for concurrency but remove the revision in the terminal result
Increment and retain a revision even after anonymisation or Customer erasure
Do not require a revision for terminal erasure
open_points.default_guess: Require the current revision, atomically perform the terminal action, and produce no next revision when the resulting model has none.

open_points.subject: Order of revision and state checks
open_points.text: A04 says a stale revision “is refused” even for a no-op, while State 0 also refuses actions because a record is archived, active, erased, unknown or otherwise ineligible.
open_points.question: When more than one condition fails, is revision checked before lifecycle and action-specific preconditions, after them, or according to a declared per-action order?
options: Authentication and existence, then lifecycle eligibility, then revision
Authentication and existence, then revision, then lifecycle eligibility
Declare a separate precedence for each action
open_points.default_guess: Check authentication and existence first, then lifecycle eligibility, then the stated revision.

open_points.subject: No-op grant or activation involving an archived project
open_points.text: A05 accepts “granting a project already in a session's set” and “making the active project active again” as no-ops; State 0 says an archived project cannot be granted or made active, while a project archived after grant or activation remains in that state.
open_points.question: If a project is already granted or active and is then archived, is repeating that grant or activation accepted as a no-op or refused because archived projects cannot be granted or made active?
options: No-op recognition takes precedence and the repeat is accepted
Archived-project refusal takes precedence
Grant repeat is accepted but active-project repeat is refused
open_points.default_guess: Apply the archived-project refusal before no-op recognition.

open_points.subject: Meaning of today for customer relationship dates
open_points.text: A05 applies R0-84's rule that an end date defaults to “today” and a later date is refused, but no calendar zone defines today.
open_points.question: Is the default and upper bound based on UTC, the owner's Europe/Madrid date, or a configured instance zone?
options: UTC date
Owner's Europe/Madrid date
Configured instance date zone
open_points.default_guess: Use the owner's Europe/Madrid calendar date because this is an owner-entered civil date.

open_points.subject: Direction of declared list orders
open_points.text: A06 says lists are “by name,” “by type,” “then by pointer id,” and identities compare as text, but explicitly states direction only for project time, artifact version and audit sequence.
open_points.question: Are all otherwise unspecified name, type, identity and registration-time components ascending, and is type compared by the same Unicode-code-point rule as names?
options: All unspecified components ascend; type uses Unicode code-point order
All identity tie-breakers ascend but type order follows the declared vocabulary
Each list may choose its own unstated direction
open_points.default_guess: Use ascending order for every unspecified component, including artifact type by Unicode code point.
